project_tracker_diagnostic: Woody-based or shrubby white composite with opposite leaves and clusters of discoid white heads; much more shrubby than herbaceous bonesets.

project_inclusion.learning_reason: Common or useful Central Texas fall/white composite for field learning.

morphology_keys.habit: Rounded shrubby plant, often woody at the base.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite, ovate to triangular-ovate, serrate, often aromatic when crushed.
morphology_keys.heads: Small white discoid heads in terminal corymbs or panicles.
morphology_keys.fna_confirmation: FNA: shrub 69–150 cm (rarely 30–200 cm), petioles 3–10(–15) mm, deltate to broadly ovate (sometimes hastate) leaves generally 3–5 × 2–5 cm; leaves essentially gland-free; involucres 4–6 mm; foliage persistent in the US flora.
morphology_keys.mature_cypsela: Hispid (hairy), contrasted with glabrous A. altissima (FNA).
morphology_keys.leaf_persistence: Persistently leaved / evergreen shrub, rare within Flora of North America Ageratina.

look_here_first: Look for a many-branched, persistent-leaved (evergreen) woody shrub with opposite, serrate, typically 3–5 cm leaves on short 3–10 mm petioles and white to faintly pinkish rayless heads. A. altissima has herbaceous stems and smoother/glabrous cypselae. Mature A. havanensis cypselae are HISPID (hairy).

comparisons.key_distinctions: Versus A. altissima: evergreen/brittle woody shrub framework (not herbaceous), shorter typical petioles, and HISPID mature cypselae (A. altissima glabrous). Versus C. odorata: A. havanensis heads have much shorter 4–6 mm involucres, compared with cylindrical 8–10 mm and 4–6+ phyllary series. Versus E. serotinum: shrub vs tall herbaceous, narrower leaves on late boneset.
